translation_notes: The site the stratifier flagged (sites[0].line == 4) is `from .namespaces import ANS`: ANS is dfriedenberger/generators' own project vocabulary object, genuinely ns_import_project -- rewritten `from generators_context import SparQLWrapper, ans:`, with ANS.hasKeyValuePair/.key/.value/.Dictionary becoming ans:hasKeyValuePair/:key/:value/:Dictionary (4 of the 7 namespace_term sites).

SAME split documented for the LexMalta/edmondchuc siblings of this stratum: RDF (`from rdflib import RDF`) is rdflib's own namespace, not a project module -- it cannot be given a __namespaces__ export, so RDF.type/RDF.Seq became `@prefix rdf: <...> .` + rdf:type/rdf:Seq instead of a prefix import (2 more of the 7 sites). classification minor-restructuring for the same reason as those siblings: two different namespace origins forced two different constructions in the same import block.

The 7th namespace_term site is process_seq's `URIRef(RDF["_{}".format(index)])`: a namespace subscript with a COMPUTED local part. Translated as `URIRef(rdf:{"_{}".format(index)})` -- terms.md's interpolated-local-part form (`ex:{name}`) -- keeping the original (redundant, since RDF[...] already returns a URIRef) outer URIRef(...) wrapper untouched, since removing it would be cleanup INSTRUCTIONS_403 forbids. Verified directly by transpiling: the interpolation's own `{}` from `"_{}".format(...)` (braces inside a string literal, inside the outer interpolation braces) does not confuse the island scanner -- emits `_ldpy_.pname(NS, ("_{}".format(index)))` correctly. This is the 1 term_constructor.

generators_context.py (shim) reconstructs ANS with a PLACEHOLDER base IRI, documented there: the real ontology file namespaces.py reads at import time (`models/assets-0.0.2.ttl`) is not part of the repository at any commit, any release, or any published sdist/wheel of `artifact-generator` (checked directly against the GitHub tree and PyPI) -- so there is no real IRI to be faithful to, only the real local names (the fragments passed to OntologyReader.get_*()). This is immaterial to correctness: no ANS.* IRI is ever returned by rdf2json.py (its output is plain JSON -- str/int/float/bool/dict/list), only used to walk the graph, so any consistent base works as long as both representations resolve through the SAME shim, verified by the driver.

oracle corrected from the mechanical draft's isomorphism to values: this region has zero .add()/.remove() -- it is pure graph reading (rdf_ops: namespace_term + term_constructor only, no triple_add/triple_remove) -- so the generic run_pair(entry=None) module-state comparison would have found no graph to compare and reported a hollow green. fixture.ttl + a custom driver (module-state's generic per-argument comparison does not special-case a SparQLWrapper the way it special-cases a bare Graph -- see driver.py) establish real equivalence: same JSON value out for the same graph in, including the zero-solutions case (ex:obj2) and a neighbourhood that must not match (ex:kv-orphan, ex:obj3).

No graph_read/trav_* island used for the .objects()/.value()/`in graph` calls, even though the region reads a graph: this region's only assigned stratum is ns_import_project (same discipline as the LexMalta sibling's own note) -- the point under test here is the import construction, and forcing m{ }/trav_* onto reads that were never in scope risks the cardinality/ordering pitfalls INSTRUCTIONS_403 §2 warns about for no measured benefit.
optimization_notes: The custom driver (fixture-values, compares process_key_value_pairs on ex:obj1 and ex:obj2, ordered) proves both optimized artefacts; the first runs failed with 'driver compared None' while the harness did not yet redirect _exec_python/_exec_ldpy to the requested sides, and the same equivalence was checked then with a scratch copy of the driver (a deliberate break, 'has_' -> 'hasx_', is detected). The fixture does not distinguish int from float values (1 == 1.0) nor a list of strings from a list of literals, so a green here is weaker on those two points.

optimized.py: unused URIRef dropped (and the redundant outer URIRef(...) around RDF[...] with it); process_seq counts with `for index in count(1)` (itertools) instead of index = 1 / index += 1, and appends process_value(...)[1] directly instead of unpacking `_, element`; `len(json_obj[key]) > 0` became the truthiness of the list; elif/else after return became plain if / raise; RDF["_{}".format(index)] became RDF[f"_{index}"]. The error paths (ValueError twice) and the None test on item are kept; value_node is kept as a variable (inlining it gives a 120-character line).

optimized.ldpy: identical outside the RDF lines: ANS/RDF/XSD terms become ans:/rdf:/xsd: prefixed names, the import of ANS becomes `from generators_context import SparQLWrapper, ans:`, RDF[f"_{index}"] becomes rdf:{f"_{index}"}. No exception to symmetry.

tried and rejected: the reads (graph.objects / graph.value / `in graph`) as m{ } islands with `@graph sparql_wrapper.graph` in each function: equivalent, but LONGER (notation ratio 1.0115 against 0.9454 for the rdflib calls), because graph.value(s, p) is already shorter than m{ {s} p ?v }.first() and the receiver costs a line per function. Fusing the two value reads of a kv_pair into one join was not done: it would silently skip a pair with no ans:value where the original raises ValueError (process_value(None)).
stratum is ns_import_project: the gain measured here is the prefixed names and the import, nothing else.

repair.driver: driver.py compare maintenant (1) les valeurs PAR TYPE (typed() : (nom du type, repr), donc int 1, float 1.0 et bool True sont trois valeurs) et (2) les ISSUES, pas seulement les valeurs (outcome() : ('returns', résultat typé) ou ('raises', classe, message), donc une ValueError retirée ou changée est une différence). Il exerce les fonctions internes en direct (process_value sur chaque noeud valeur des deux graphes, process_seq sur chaque rdf:Seq et sur un non-liste, literal_to_value sur 16 littéraux construits en Python) en plus de process_key_value_pairs sur 4 ancres qui rendent et 12 ancres ex:err-* qui lèvent. fixture.ttl reçoit : ex:obj-types (xsd:integer incl. 0 et négatif, xsd:float incl. 0.0, 2 entier, NaN, INF, xsd:boolean true/false/0/1, quatre chaines sans datatype dont '' et '42', une langue), ex:obj-lists (rdf:Seq vide, liste typée, membres faux '' / 0 / false / 0.0 qui ne doivent pas arrêter la marche, douze membres lus par numéro, un trou, liste contenant liste et dictionnaire, noeud à la fois rdf:Seq et ans:Dictionary, dictionnaire vide) et les ancres d'erreur (xsd:string, xsd:date, xsd:double, xsd:decimal, IRI nue, noeud anonyme nu, xsd:integer/xsd:float mal formés, et les mêmes erreurs levées depuis un dictionnaire et une liste imbriqués). fixture_missing.ttl (nouveau, sans rdf:Seq : dans fixture.ttl `(None, rdf:type, rdf:Seq) in graph` est un joker) porte les paires sans ans:value, sans ans:key, sans rien.
